rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine form with ta marbuta marks one occurrence: Abraham made this promise once; وعد and موعد do not themselves imply a single occurrence.
rows.anchor: موعدة على أوزان المرّة لأن أحياناً المصدر الثلاثي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's one-time promise does not license Muslims or prophets to seek forgiveness for a disbelieving parent; God forbade repeating it.
rows.anchor: ليس لك حق أن تستغفر لأبيك الكافر، لا يجوز، هذا ليس لكم فيه أسوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone is driven, but the destination is the point: unbelievers go to Hell and the God-fearing to Paradise; the Qur'an likewise says each soul has a driver and witness.
rows.anchor: إذن كلهم يساقون لكن المهم جهة السوق فهؤلاء يُساق بهم إلى الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw before the statement that the stars are subjected by His command either coordinates one sentence with another or is resumptive.
rows.anchor: الواو إما عطف جملة على جملة وإما إستئنافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic noun niʿma with kasra consistently refers to a good or blessing.
rows.anchor: دائماً تأتي في الخير في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell's gates are normally shut and opening them at arrival startles and terrifies; Paradise's gates are always open, unlike a prison's.
rows.anchor: والفارق أن جهنم هي كالسجن أبوابها مقفلة لا تفتح إلا لداخل أو خارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise's residents move freely, and those approaching can see it ahead, so God lets them feel joy in their reward before entering.
rows.anchor: وأهلها يتنقلون فيها من مكان إلى آخر في يسر وسرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hell conditional has an explicit answer; the Paradise conditional has none because human language cannot encompass its blessings, whose answer lies within Paradise.
rows.anchor: أما في حال الجنة فلا يوجد جواب للشرط لأنه يضيق ذكر النعمة

words: يعذب من يشاء ويغفر لمن يشاء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishment appropriately precedes forgiveness in 5:40 because the context concerns violent rebels and thieves, making a warning and deterrent apt.
rows.anchor: وردت في سياق ذكر قطاع الطرق والمحاربين والسرّاق كان المناسب تقديم ذكر العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 29:56, possessives for God's servants and land plus إن emphasize the land's vastness; 39:10 says God's earth is vast without extra emphasis because it is unnecessary there.
rows.anchor: العباد عباده والأرض أرضه ولإضافة الياء إلى كلمة

words: كل نفس ذائقة الموت ثم إلينا ترجعون
إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى الصَّابِرُونَ أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universal death and return statement fits the broad address to God's servants in Ankabut, while the few patient people in Zumar fit its narrower class of servants.
rows.anchor: الصابرون هم قلة فناسب سياق الآية كلها الطبقة القليلة مع عباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ankabut repeats first-person divine pronouns five times in the passage, while Zumar's address omits the possessive first-person suffix.
rows.anchor: ضمير المتكلم تكرر 5 مرات في سورة العنكبوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ankabut maintains first-person divine speech through its context; Zumar uses indirect third-person relay through قل, a pattern that continues through its two procession verses.
rows.anchor: آية سورة العنكبوت مبنية على التكلّم بينما آية سورة الزمر مبنية على الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun comes first in Ankabut because the preceding verse calls earlier peoples discerning; Qarun knew the truth as one of Moses's people but rebelled.
rows.anchor: قارون كان مستبصراً فقد كان من قوم موسى فبغى عليهم أي أنه كان يعرف الحق مستبصراً به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ankabut orders Qarun before Pharaoh to match the punishment sequence: Qarun was swallowed by the earth before Pharaoh was drowned.
rows.anchor: ثم إن الترتيب جاء مناسباً لترتيب العقوبة في السورة عقاب قارون أولاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghafir puts Pharaoh first because Moses was sent to him and the sura then focuses on him; Qarun is outside that context.
rows.anchor: لمن أرسل موسى؟ لفرعون فناسب أن يكون فرعون أول المذكورين في الآية التي بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guests greet Abraham with a verbal clause and he replies with a nominal clause, which the author says is stronger, more lasting, and more eloquent, showing extra courtesy.
rows.anchor: الجملة الإسمية أقوى لغوياً وأثبت للمعنى وأبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham calls them strangers generally instead of addressing them directly, which is courteous; Lot uses direct address while in a crisis.
rows.anchor: قال (قوم منكرون) ولم يقل إنكم قوم منكرون لكن عندما رآهم قال قوم غرباء بشكل عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāgha means Abraham went secretly without showing where he was going; bringing a fat calf likewise honors his guests.
rows.anchor: راغ معناها أنه ذهب بخفية ولم يرد أن يظهر أنه ذهب وهذا من إكرام الضيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing the food close and inviting the guests to eat are further signs of honoring them.
rows.anchor: وهذا أيضاً من باب الإكرام أن قرّب لهم الطعام وقال ألا تأكلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham openly expresses fear, and that fear has spread through the whole household.
rows.anchor: ظهر عليه الخوف هنا وعمّ الخوف أهل البيت جميعاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham keeps his fear from his guests as a courtesy; Moses's fear also remains unshown because he faces Pharaoh and his people.
rows.anchor: لم يرد إبراهيم أن يطلعهم على خوفه وهذا من مظاهر التكريم

words: لا توجل إنا نبشرك بغلام عليم
أبشرتموني على أن مسني الكبر فبم تبشرون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guests answer Abraham's declared fear with glad tidings; because fear had made him suspect them, he asks how they can announce a son despite his old age.
rows.anchor: واعترف إبراهيم أنه يشك فيهم مما بلغه من الخوف فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the other account Abraham does not question the announcement: objection would violate the courtesy due to his guests, so he does not doubt them.
rows.anchor: لم يعترض إبراهيم هنا لأن الإعتراض ليس من مقام الإكرام فلم يشك في قولهم ولا اعترض عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account omits Abraham's wife because fear overwhelms the entire household, so she does not come out to face the guests.
rows.anchor: لم يذكر امرأة إبراهيم لأن الخوف هنا كان طاغياً على البيت كله وأهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥilm is the ability to control oneself when angry, visible in how one treats other people.
rows.anchor: الحلم هو أن يملك الإنسان نفسه عند الغضب وهذا يظهر في علاقته مع الآخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael's conduct toward his father during the sacrifice and their house-building, together with his fidelity in conveying the message, supports his characteristic forbearance; the Qur'an does not similarly describe Isaac's social relations.
rows.anchor: كذلك الحلم في علاقته مع أبيه في بناء البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A named prophetic quality is prominent, not exclusive: all prophets turn to God, while Ishmael's standout forbearance is inherited from Abraham; this does not imply other prophets lack it.
rows.anchor: الصفة البارزة في إسماعيل - عليه السلام - هي الحلم وقد أخذها عن أبيه إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael's glad tidings came directly from God, whereas Isaac's were delivered by angels rather than directly to Abraham by God.
rows.anchor: جاءت البشارة مباشرة من الله تعالى كما ورد في آية سورة الصافات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dunuww means closeness from either direction, while tadallī is only downward from above; Gabriel's descent toward the Prophet is therefore an honor.
rows.anchor: الدنو غير التدلي فالدنو هو القرب من أسفل إلى أعلى أو من أعلى إلى أسفل وغيره أما التدلّي فلا يكون إلا من أعلى لأسفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bow image conveys closeness while evoking strength, a taut bowstring, an accurate strong archer, and the elements of the journey described in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: القوس يحتاج إلى إحكام في التسديد والإنطلاق وهذه كلها عناصر الرحلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbd refers to body and spirit together, so this wording affirms a bodily as well as spiritual Isra and Mi'raj; otherwise the disbelievers would not have denied the miracle.
rows.anchor: تستخدم كلمة (عبد) على مجموع الجسد والروح وهنا إثبات على أن الإسراء والمعراج كان بالروح والجسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fuʾād evokes heat and intensity, as in roasting meat; the Prophet's alert heart confirmed his sight and did not mistake it for illusion, so what he saw was true.
rows.anchor: اختيار لفظ الفؤاد هو من التفؤد والتوقّد (يقال فأد اللحم بمعنى شواه)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word sariyy means a master or nobleman; its plural is surāt, supported by the cited line about nobles when the ignorant rule.
rows.anchor: وهي تعني السيّد وجمعها سُراة أي السادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whenever Qur'anic wording pairs eating with drinking, eating comes first because obtaining food is harder than obtaining drink, including in Paradise.
rows.anchor: حيثما اجتمع الأكل والشرب قدّم تعالى الأكل على الشرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud 11:28 puts mercy before the prepositional phrase because the surrounding pronouns and clauses refer back to that mercy.
rows.anchor: والآية تتكلم عن الرحمة (فعمّيت، أنلزمكموها، وأنتم لها كارهون) كلها تعود على الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud 11:63 puts minhu before mercy because the passage focuses on God through references to the Lord, God, Him, and disobeying Him.
rows.anchor: الآية تتكلم عن الله تعالى (ربي، الله، منه، الضمير في عصيته) كلها تعود على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud 11:28 places mercy before the prepositional phrase because the verse's later clauses focus on mercy.
rows.anchor: في الآية الأولى قدّم الرحمة على الجارّ والمجرور، والآية تتكلم عن الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud 11:63 places minhu first because its context repeatedly refers to God, including as Lord, God, and the one disobeyed.
rows.anchor: أما في الآية الثانية فالآية تتكلم عن الله تعالى (ربي، الله، منه، الضمير في عصيته)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an varies word order across parallel expressions; explaining fronting requires identifying the contextual focus, rather than merely asserting emphasis.
rows.anchor: ولا ينبغي الإكتفاء بالإهتمام لتفسير التقديم والتأخير في القرآن بل يجب أن يُعرف سياق الآيات ودلالتها على الإهتمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-karh with fatḥa means coercion imposed from outside, contrasted with voluntary action; the source illustrates it with forced inheritance, spending, and the address to heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: الكَره) - بفتح الكاف - هو ما يأتي من الخارج يقابله الطوع
